questions.question: In October 2024, which of the following state governments launched India’s first integrated state-level Cyber Command and Control Centre to serve as a comprehensive hub for handling grievances through multiple channels, including a helpline, web portal and mobile app?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **October 2024**, the **Maharashtra** government inaugurated India’s first integrated state-level **Cyber Command and Control Centre (C4)** at **Mahape, Navi Mumbai**.
 
• The facility was officially launched by the Deputy Chief Minister of **Maharashtra**, **Devendra Fadnavis**, who also holds the Home portfolio.
 
• This center serves as a comprehensive hub for handling cybercrime grievances through multiple channels, including the national **helpline 1930**, a dedicated **web portal**, and a **mobile application**.
 
• The project is part of a larger initiative to modernize the state's police force and provides a single-window system for citizens to report digital frauds, phishing, and other cyber-related offenses.
 
• The **C4** is equipped with advanced technology to ensure **24/7 monitoring** and faster response times for cyber incidents across the state. ***Hence, the correct answer is Maharashtra.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Maharashtra Cyber Security Project:**
 
 
• The **Cyber Command and Control Centre** is a core component of the **Maharashtra Cyber Security Project**, which has an estimated budget of approximately **Rs 837 crore**.
 
• The project was executed with **Larsen & Toubro (L&T)** as the primary technology partner, ensuring the deployment of world-class digital infrastructure.
 
• It aims to integrate all **district-level cyber labs** into a centralized system for better coordination and data sharing among law enforcement agencies.
 
 
 
• **Technological Features:**
 
 
• The center utilizes **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **Machine Learning (ML)** tools to track financial trails in cyber frauds and predict emerging digital threats.
 
• It houses a **Cert-Maharashtra** (Computer Emergency Response Team) and a **Centre of Excellence** to train police personnel in the latest investigation techniques.
 
• The facility includes specialized units for **digital forensics**, **social media monitoring**, and **threat intelligence**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Human Resources:** The center is staffed by over **150 cyber experts** and specially trained **Maharashtra State Police** personnel to manage complex investigations.
 
• **Public Safety:** With the rise in digital transactions, the center focuses on reducing the "golden hour" response time to freeze fraudulent transactions before the money is moved out of the banking system.
 
• **National Context:** While various states have cyber cells, **Maharashtra** is the first to implement such a massive, integrated **state-level** command structure, setting a benchmark for the **Government of India**’s digital security framework.
 
• **Launch Date:** The formal inauguration took place on **October 10, 2024**, marking a significant milestone in India's fight against trans-border and domestic cybercrimes.

questions.question: Which of the following parties won 5 seats in the Bihar Assembly elections 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindustani Awam Morcha (Secular)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hindustani Awam Morcha (Secular)**, often abbreviated as **HAM-S**, is a regional political party in the state of **Bihar**, India. In the context of the **Bihar Assembly Elections 2025**, the party successfully secured **5 seats**.
 
• The party was founded by **Jitan Ram Manjhi**, a former **Chief Minister of Bihar**, on **May 8, 2015**, after he left the **Janata Dal (United)**.
 
• The party primarily represents the interests of the **Mahadalit** community and other marginalized sections in **Bihar**. It has been a part of various political alliances, including the **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)** and the **Mahagathbandhan**.
 
• The **Bihar Legislative Assembly** (Vidhan Sabha) has a total of **243 seats**. To form a government, a party or a coalition must cross the majority mark of **122 seats**. Small regional parties like **HAM-S** often play the role of "kingmaker" in close electoral contests.
 
• In the **2025 elections**, the performance of smaller parties proved crucial in determining the power dynamics of the state's governance. Winning **5 seats** allowed **HAM-S** to maintain its relevance in the state's competitive political landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Janata Dal (United) (JD-U):**
 
 
• The **JD(U)** is a major regional party in **Bihar**, currently led by **Nitish Kumar**. The party's symbol is an **Arrow**. It has held the **Chief Minister's** post for the majority of the last two decades.
 
 
 
• **Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) (LJP-RV):**
 
 
• Led by **Chirag Paswan**, this party was formed following a split in the original **Lok Janshakti Party** (LJP) founded by **Ram Vilas Paswan**. The party's election symbol is the **Helicopter**. It focuses on the **Dalit** and **Paswan** vote bank in **Bihar**.
 
 
 
• **Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP):**
 
 
• The **BSP** is a national party led by **Mayawati**. While its primary base is in **Uttar Pradesh**, it regularly contests elections in **Bihar** to mobilize **Scheduled Caste** voters. Its symbol is the **Elephant**.
 
 
 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI):**
 
 
• The **ECI** is the constitutional body responsible for conducting elections to the **Bihar Legislative Assembly**. It operates under **Article 324** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Reserved Seats:** Out of the total seats, **38 seats** are reserved for **Scheduled Castes (SC)** and **2 seats** are reserved for **Scheduled Tribes (ST)** in the **Bihar Vidhan Sabha**.
 
• **Voter Turnout:** Elections in **Bihar** typically see high engagement from rural voters, with the **Election Commission** implementing various initiatives to increase the participation of **women** and **youth**.
 
• **Regional Alliances:** The **2025** political landscape was shaped by the two main fronts: the **NDA** (led by **BJP** and **JD-U**) and the **Mahagathbandhan** (led by **RJD** and **INC**).

questions.question: Which student-led national case competition launched in October 2025 aims to address malnutrition and promotes SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) and SDG 3 (Good Health & Well-being)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yukti – Nutrition Nirmaan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Yukti – Nutrition Nirmaan** is a premier student-led national case competition officially launched in **October 2025** to address the complex challenges of **malnutrition** in India.
 
• The initiative is strategically designed to align with and promote **Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger)** and **Sustainable Development Goal 3 (Good Health & Well-being)**.
 
• The competition aims to harness the creative and analytical potential of students from diverse academic backgrounds to propose **innovative, scalable, and sustainable solutions** for improving nutritional outcomes.
 
• By focusing on **malnutrition**, the program targets various facets of the issue, including **undernutrition, micronutrient deficiencies**, and the rising trend of **overweight and obesity** among different age groups.
 
• Participants are encouraged to develop **interdisciplinary strategies** that combine public policy, technology, and community-level interventions to ensure a **malnutrition-free India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 2 (SDG 2):**
 
 
• Known as **Zero Hunger**, this goal aims to end hunger, achieve **food security**, and improve **nutrition** globally by the year **2030**.
 
• It emphasizes doubling the **agricultural productivity** and incomes of small-scale food producers to ensure sustainable food production systems.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 3 (SDG 3):**
 
 
• This goal focuses on **Good Health and Well-being**, ensuring healthy lives and promoting well-being for all at all ages.
 
• Proper **nutrition** is considered a foundational pillar for achieving the targets under this goal, as it directly impacts maternal and child mortality rates.
 
 
 
• **The Challenge of Malnutrition:**
 
 
• Malnutrition remains a critical public health concern, manifesting as **stunting** (low height-for-age), **wasting** (low weight-for-height), and **anemia**.
 
• According to various health surveys, including **NFHS-5**, a significant percentage of **children under 5 years** and **women of reproductive age** in India suffer from nutritional deficiencies.
 
 
 
• **Youth-Led Initiatives:**
 
 
• Competitions like **Yukti** empower the **youth** to transition from passive learners to active problem solvers in the national development agenda.
 
• These platforms serve as a bridge between **Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs)** and government bodies to foster **evidence-based policy making**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **POSHAN Abhiyaan:** The **Prime Minister's Overarching Scheme for Holistic Nourishment**, launched in **2018**, provides the overarching framework for nutrition-related interventions that competitions like **Yukti** seek to augment.
 
• **Triple Burden of Malnutrition:** Modern nutritional challenges include the coexistence of **undernutrition**, **micronutrient deficiencies** (hidden hunger), and **overnutrition** (obesity), all of which require tailored solutions.
 
• **Viksit Bharat @ 2047:** Addressing health and nutrition is a key component of the vision to make India a **developed nation** by the **100th year of Independence**.
 
• **Technological Integration:** Modern solutions often involve the use of **Data Analytics, AI, and mobile platforms** to monitor nutritional delivery and identify **malnutrition hotspots** in real-time.

questions.question: Which important day commemorating India’s victory over Pakistan was observed on 26 July 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kargil Vijay Diwas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kargil Vijay Diwas** is observed every year on **July 26** to commemorate the victory of the **Indian Armed Forces** over **Pakistan** in the **Kargil War** of **1999**.
 
• The day marks the successful conclusion of **Operation Vijay**, during which **India** regained control of the high outposts in the **Kargil-Dras** sector that had been illegally occupied by **Pakistani** intruders.
 
• The **Kargil War** lasted for more than **60 days**, starting in **May 1999** and officially ending on **July 26, 1999**, when **Pakistan** was completely evicted from **Indian** territory.
 
• On **26 July 2025**, **India** observed the **26th anniversary** of this historic victory, paying tribute to the **527 soldiers** who made the supreme sacrifice for the nation.
 
• The main celebrations are typically held at the **Kargil War Memorial** located in **Dras**, **Ladakh**, which is often referred to as the second coldest inhabited place in the world. ***Hence, the correct answer is Kargil Vijay Diwas.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Important National Days:**
 
 
• **Republic Day**: Observed on **26 January** every year, it commemorates the date on which the **Constitution of India** came into effect in **1950**.
 
• **Independence Day**: Observed on **15 August**, it marks **India's** freedom from **British** rule in **1947**.
 
• **Border Security Day**: While **1 December** is celebrated as the **BSF Raising Day**, **Kargil Vijay Diwas** specifically focuses on the joint military victory in the **Kargil** sector.
 
 
 
• **The Kargil Conflict:**
 
 
• The war was fought at high altitudes ranging from **11,000 to 18,000 feet**, making it one of the most difficult mountain warfare operations in history.
 
• **Operation Safed Sagar**: This was the code name assigned to the **Indian Air Force's** role in acting jointly with the **Indian Army** during the conflict.
 
• **Operation Talwar**: This was the **Indian Navy's** blockade of **Pakistani** ports (specifically **Karachi**) during the war to cut off supply lines.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Heroes of Kargil:** Several soldiers were awarded the **Param Vir Chakra**, India's highest military decoration, including **Captain Vikram Batra**, **Lieutenant Manoj Kumar Pandey**, **Rifleman Sanjay Kumar**, and **Grenadier Yogendra Singh Yadav**.
 
• **Political Leadership:** During the **1999** war, **Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee** was the **Prime Minister of India**, and **George Fernandes** served as the **Defence Minister**.
 
• **Geographic Location:** The conflict took place in the **Kargil district** of **Ladakh**, along the **Line of Control (LoC)**. Strategic peaks like **Tiger Hill** and **Tololing** were key battlegrounds.
 
• **Global Significance:** The **Kargil War** was the first direct conventional war between two **nuclear-armed** nations, drawing significant international attention and diplomatic pressure on **Pakistan** to withdraw.
</ul

questions.question: Where was the Senior Asian Wrestling Championship 2025 held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jordan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Senior Asian Wrestling Championship 2025** was designated to be hosted in **Amman**, the capital city of **Jordan**.
 
• The event was scheduled to take place from **March 25** to **March 30**, **2025**, bringing together elite wrestlers from across the **Asian continent**.
 
• This prestigious tournament is organized under the aegis of **United World Wrestling (UWW) Asia**, which is the continental governing body for the sport.
 
• The championship typically features three primary disciplines of wrestling: **Men's Freestyle**, **Men's Greco-Roman**, and **Women's Freestyle**.
 
• **Jordan** has increasingly become a preferred destination for international wrestling, having successfully hosted the **U20 World Wrestling Championships** in **2023** and the **U17** and **U23 Asian Championships** in **2024**.
 
• Hosting the **Senior Asian Wrestling Championship** is a significant milestone for **Jordan**, reinforcing its position as a growing hub for combat sports in the **West Asia** region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **United World Wrestling (UWW)**:
 
 
• It is the international governing body for the sport of amateur wrestling, headquartered in **Corsier-sur-Vevey**, **Switzerland**.
 
• The organization was formerly known as **FILA** (Fédération Internationale des Luttes Associées) until its rebranding in **2014**.
 
 
 
• **History of Asian Wrestling Championships**:
 
 
• The **Asian Wrestling Championships** first commenced in **1979** for men's freestyle and Greco-Roman events.
 
• Women's wrestling was officially integrated into the championship program in **1996**, highlighting the growth of the sport among female athletes in **Asia**.
 
 
 
• **Previous Host (2024)**:
 
 
• The **2024** edition of the **Senior Asian Wrestling Championships** was held in **Bishkek**, **Kyrgyzstan**, in **April 2024**.
 
• Countries like **Japan**, **Iran**, **Kazakhstan**, and **India** are historically the dominant forces in these continental championships.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Event**:
 
 
• The championships are crucial for athletes to gain **UWW World Ranking** points, which determine seeding for major global events such as the **World Championships** and the **Olympic Games**.
 
• The tournament serves as a platform to showcase the technical prowess of **Asian** wrestlers, who currently hold numerous world and Olympic titles.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What is the name of the new defence facility inaugurated by Rajnath Singh in New Delhi in November 2025?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Defence Minister Rajnath Singh** inaugurated **DPSU Bhawan**, a dedicated office complex for **Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs)**, in **New Delhi** in **November 2024**.
 
• The facility is located at **Kasturba Gandhi Marg** and serves as a centralized hub to facilitate better coordination between the **Ministry of Defence** and various **DPSUs**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the inauguration of DPSU Bhawan is correct.***
 
• The **DPSU Bhawan** is designed to provide a **collaborative workspace** for the executives and liaison officers of different defence production entities under one roof.
 
• The building is equipped with **modern amenities**, meeting rooms, and high-tech communication systems to streamline **administrative functions** and decision-making processes.
 
• This initiative is part of the government's broader vision to enhance **ease of doing business** within the defence sector and promote **synergy** among the **seven new defence companies** and older establishments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs):**
 
 
• There are several **DPSUs** in India, including giants like **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)**, **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)**, and **Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL)**.
 
• In **October 2021**, the government dissolved the **Ordnance Factory Board (OFB)** and converted its **41 factories** into **seven new DPSUs** to improve efficiency and competitiveness.
 
• These seven companies include **Munitions India Limited (MIL)**, **Armoured Vehicles Nigam Limited (AVANI)**, and **Advanced Weapons and Equipment India Limited (AWE India)**.
 
 
 
• **Aatmanirbharta in Defence:**
 
 
• The **Ministry of Defence** has set a target of achieving a **defence manufacturing turnover** of **Rs 1.75 lakh crore** by **2024-25**.
 
• India's **defence exports** reached a record high of over **Rs 21,000 crore** in the financial year **2023-24**, showcasing the success of the **'Make in India'** program.
 
• Positive **Indigenisation Lists** have been notified by the government to ban the import of several hundred items, encouraging local production by **DPSUs** and private players.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Significance:** The **DPSU Bhawan** symbolizes the shift towards a more **corporate culture** within government-owned defence entities, focusing on **profitability** and **global standards**.
 
• **Infrastructure:** The building was constructed with a focus on **sustainability**, adhering to **Green Building** norms to minimize environmental impact in the heart of the **National Capital**.
 
• **Operational Efficiency:** By bringing liaison offices to a single location, the **Ministry of Defence** aims to reduce **red tape** and accelerate the procurement and production timelines for **Armed Forces** requirements.
</ul

questions.question: In April 2025, which international organisation acknowledged India’s achievement in lifting 171 million people out of extreme poverty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **April 2025**, the **World Bank** officially acknowledged India's significant milestone in poverty reduction, noting that the country lifted **171 million people** out of **extreme poverty**.
 
• The **World Bank** report highlighted that India's achievement is one of the fastest reductions in poverty globally, driven by sustained **economic growth** and targeted **social welfare programs**.
 
• Key contributors to this success include the massive expansion of **Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI)**, which enabled the seamless delivery of **Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT)** to the most vulnerable populations.
 
• The international financial institution praised the effectiveness of schemes like the **Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY)**, which provided **food security** to over **800 million citizens**, preventing a slide back into poverty during global economic shocks.
 
• This recognition underscores India's progress toward achieving **Sustainable Development Goal 1 (SDG 1)**, which aims to end poverty in all its forms everywhere by **2030**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Bank Group:**
 
 
• The **World Bank** was established in **1944** at the **Bretton Woods Conference** and is headquartered in **Washington, D.C.**, **USA**.
 
• It consists of two main institutions: the **International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)** and the **International Development Association (IDA)**.
 
• Its primary mission is to provide **loans**, **grants**, and **technical assistance** to developing countries to reduce **poverty** and promote **shared prosperity**.
 
 
 
• **Extreme Poverty Line:**
 
 
• The **World Bank** defines **extreme poverty** as living on less than **$2.15 per person per day**, based on **2017 Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** prices.
 
• This international poverty line is used to monitor global progress toward the elimination of severe economic deprivation.
 
 
 
• **Other International Organizations:**
 
 
• **United Nations (UN):** An intergovernmental organization founded in **1945** to maintain international peace and security and achieve international cooperation.
 
• **International Monetary Fund (IMF):** Also founded in **1944**, it focuses on **global monetary cooperation**, **financial stability**, and **international trade**.
 
• **Asian Development Bank (ADB):** Established in **1966** and headquartered in **Manila**, **Philippines**, it focuses on social and economic development in **Asia and the Pacific**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Poverty Measurement in India:** While the **World Bank** uses the **$2.15** line, India also uses the **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**, tracked by **NITI Aayog**, which considers health, education, and standard of living.
 
• **Impact of Digitization:** India's **JAM Trinity** (**Jan Dhan** accounts, **Aadhaar**, and **Mobile** connectivity) has been cited by the **World Bank** as a global model for **financial inclusion**.
 
• **Historical Context:** India has historically been home to a large number of the world's poor, but rapid **GDP growth** since the **1991 reforms** and recent **welfare innovations** have drastically changed the demographic landscape.
 
• **Global Poverty Reports:** The **World Bank** periodically releases the **Poverty and Shared Prosperity Report**, providing the latest data on global trends and the impact of policy interventions.
</ul

questions.question: Before the approval of caste census in 2025, the last major attempt to gather caste-based data at the national level was made through which exercise?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC), 2011**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC)** was launched in **June 2011** across all **States and Union Territories** of India.
 
• It represented the first major effort to collect detailed caste data at a national scale since the **1931 Census**, which was the last time caste-wide data was fully enumerated in British India.
 
• The **SECC 2011** was not conducted under the **Census Act of 1948**, but rather as a separate administrative exercise to identify beneficiaries for welfare schemes.
 
• It was carried out through three different agencies: the **Ministry of Rural Development** (for rural areas), the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation** (for urban areas), and the **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner** (for the caste and religious enumeration).
 
• The primary objective was to rank households based on their **socio-economic status** using specific **deprivation indicators**, enabling the government to target subsidies and social security benefits more effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Decennial Census of India:**
 
 
• The regular **Census of India** is conducted every **10 years** by the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.
 
• Since independence, the regular census has only published data for **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)**, avoiding a comprehensive count of **Other Backward Classes (OBCs)** or general castes.
 
• The last completed regular census took place in **2011**, while the **2021 Census** was delayed due to the **COVID-19 pandemic**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Census:**
 
 
• This exercise focuses on the structure and activities of **entrepreneurial units** (both agricultural and non-agricultural) in the country.
 
• The **first Economic Census** was conducted in **1977**, and the **seventh** was initiated in **2019**. It does not primarily collect caste-based demographic data.
 
 
 
• **National Sample Survey (NSS):**
 
 
• The **NSSO** (now part of the **National Statistical Office - NSO**) conducts periodic surveys on **employment**, **consumer expenditure**, and **literacy**.
 
• While it provides statistical estimates regarding caste groups (like **OBCs**), it is based on **sampling** rather than a 100% headcount of the population.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Data Publication:** Although the **SECC 2011** data regarding **socio-economic indicators** was released in **July 2015**, the specific **caste data** was withheld by the government, citing technical flaws and classification complexities.
 
• **Mandal Commission:** In the absence of modern caste data, the **Mandal Commission (1979)** used the **1931 Census** figures to estimate the **OBC** population at **52%**.
 
• **State Initiatives:** Due to the delay in a national caste census, states like **Bihar** conducted their own **Caste-based Survey** in **2023**, which reported that **Extremely Backward Classes (EBCs)** and **OBCs** together constitute over **63%** of the state's population.
 
• **2025 Outlook:** The central government has indicated that the next **Decennial Census**, likely beginning in **2025**, may incorporate new methodologies or categories to address the long-standing demand for updated **caste statistics**.
</ul

questions.question: Who, as a digital content creator, co-founded Monk Entertainment and was a prominent figure in 2025?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question: Who conferred awards to cities under the Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan Awards 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Environment Minister, GoI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The awards for the **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan** (Clean Air Survey) are typically conferred by the **Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**.
 
• For the year **2024-2025**, the awards recognize cities that have made significant improvements in air quality and implemented effective measures under the **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)**.
 
• The ceremony is usually organized on **September 7**, which marks the **International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies**, an initiative by the **United Nations**.
 
• The **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan** ranks **131 cities** across the country into three categories based on population: **Category 1** (above 10 lakh), **Category 2** (3 to 10 lakh), and **Category 3** (less than 3 lakh).
 
• The ranking is based on self-assessment reports submitted by cities on the **PRANA portal**, which are then vetted by the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP):**
 
 
• Launched in **January 2019**, it is a long-term, time-bound, national-level strategy to tackle the air pollution problem across the **country**.
 
• The original target was to achieve a **20% to 30% reduction** in **Particulate Matter (PM10 and PM2.5)** concentrations by **2024**, taking **2017** as the base year.
 
• The goal was later updated to achieve a **40% reduction** in particulate matter concentrations by the year **2026**.
 
 
 
• **Assessment Parameters:**
 
 
• Cities are evaluated on **eight thematic areas**, including control of **biomass and municipal solid waste burning**, road dust management, **construction and demolition waste**, vehicular emissions, and industrial pollution.
 
• Public awareness programs and improvements in **PM10 concentrations** carry significant weightage in the final score.
 
 
 
• **PRANA Portal:**
 
 
• **PRANA** stands for **Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities**.
 
• It is a platform used to monitor the implementation of the **NCAP** and track the progress of city-specific **Action Plans**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ministerial Role:** The **Environment Minister**, currently **Shri Bhupender Yadav** (as of the recent sessions), plays a pivotal role in steering the **MoEFCC** towards sustainable urban development and pollution control.
 
• **Top Performing Cities:** In recent cycles, cities like **Indore**, **Agra**, **Thane**, and **Surat** have consistently secured top positions in **Category 1** for their exemplary air quality management.
 
• **Non-Attainment Cities:** These are **131 cities** that consistently failed to meet the **National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)** for over five years. The **NCAP** specifically targets these urban centers to ensure healthier breathing conditions for **millions of citizens**.
 
• **Global Context:** The **International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies** was established by the **UN General Assembly** in **2019** to emphasize the need for international cooperation to improve air quality globally.
</ul

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bagori Range**, also famously known as the **Western Range** of **Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve**, was officially announced to be the first range to open for the **2025–26 tourist season** in **September 2025**.
 
• Traditionally, the **Bagori Range** is preferred for the early start of the season because its tracks and terrain usually dry up faster after the **monsoon floods** compared to the central or eastern sectors.
 
• The opening of the park generally occurs in a phased manner, starting with **Jeep Safaris** in the **Bagori** and **Kohora** ranges, while **Elephant Safaris** are introduced later once the ground is sufficiently firm.
 
• This announcement is crucial for the tourism industry in **Assam**, as the park remains closed from **May** to **September** every year due to the overflow of the **Brahmaputra River**.
 
• The **Bagori Range** is highly popular among tourists specifically for sightings of the **Great Indian One-Horned Rhinoceros**, as the visibility in this grassland-dominated range is exceptionally high.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kaziranga National Park**: Located in the **Golaghat** and **Nagaon** districts of the state of **Assam**, **India**. It was established as a **Reserve Forest** in **1905**, declared a **National Park** in **1974**, and designated a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1985**.
 
• **The Big Five**: The park is globally recognized for conserving five major species: the **One-Horned Rhinoceros** (hosting over **2,600** individuals), the **Royal Bengal Tiger**, the **Asian Elephant**, the **Wild Water Buffalo**, and the **Eastern Swamp Deer** (Barasingha).
 
• **Tiger Reserve Status**: It was declared a **Tiger Reserve** in **2006** and currently holds one of the highest densities of tigers in the world.
 
• **Geographical Features**: The park is situated on the edge of the **Eastern Himalaya** biodiversity hotspot and is bounded by the **Brahmaputra River** to the north and the **Karbi Anglong Hills** to the south. It covers a core area of approximately **430 square kilometers**.
 
• **Flora and Avifauna**: The vegetation consists of **tall elephant grass**, marshland, and dense tropical moist broadleaf forests. It is also an **Important Bird Area (IBA)**, home to over **478 species** of birds, including migratory species from **Central Asia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bagori Range (Western Range)**: This is the primary choice for **Jeep Safaris** and is known for its high-density population of **Rhinos**. It is located in the **Nagaon** district side of the park. ***Hence, it is the correct answer.***
 
• **Kohora Range (Central Range)**: This range is the administrative hub of the park. It is the most visited range and is the primary location for **Elephant Safaris**. However, it was not the first to be announced for the **2025–26** season. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
• **Agaratoli Range (Eastern Range)**: Located in the **Golaghat** district, this range is famous for **bird watching** and **Wild Water Buffaloes**. It usually opens slightly later than the Western range due to its proximity to the **Brahmaputra**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
• **Burapahar Range (Ghorakati)**: This range is situated at the edge of the hills and is excellent for spotting primates like the **Hoolock Gibbon** and the **Capped Langur**. It offers trekking opportunities which are unique to this sector. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
• **Conservation History**: The park's protection began after **Mary Curzon**, the wife of the **Viceroy of India**, **Lord Curzon**, visited the area in **1904** and failed to see a single rhinoceros, prompting immediate conservation measures.

questions.question: In which union territory of India was the world’s highest rail arch bridge inaugurated by the Prime Minister of India in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jammu and Kashmir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The world’s highest rail arch bridge, known as the **Chenab Bridge**, is located in the **Reasi** district of the Union Territory of **Jammu and Kashmir**.
 
• The bridge stands at a staggering height of **359 meters** (approximately **1,178 feet**) above the river bed, making it **35 meters taller** than the **Eiffel Tower** in **Paris**.
 
• It was inaugurated for full-scale operations as part of the **Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL)** project, a massive infrastructure undertaking by the **Indian Railways** to provide all-weather connectivity to the **Kashmir Valley**.
 
• The bridge spans the **Chenab River** between **Bakkal** and **Kauri**. It is a structural marvel designed to withstand high-velocity winds of up to **266 kmph** and extreme temperatures.
